title: NAFEMS FV2 pin-ended double cross, in-plane vibration (planar beams in a 2D model)
source: NAFEMS, The Standard NAFEMS Benchmarks, TNSB Rev. 3, October 1990, test FV2 (frequencies 11.336 Hz mode 1, 17.709 Hz modes 2-8, 45.345 Hz mode 9, 57.390 Hz modes 10-16); from F. Abbassian, D. J. Dawswell, N. C. Knowles, Selected Benchmarks for Natural Frequency Analysis, NAFEMS 1987, test 2

quantities.reason: NAFEMS's targets are Euler-Bernoulli values (pinned-pinned and clamped-pinned arms: lambda^2/(2 pi L^2) sqrt(E I/(rho A)), lambda = pi, 3.9266, 2 pi, 7.0686), without shear deformation or rotary inertia; the Timoshenko element has both, which lowers a pinned-pinned arm by 0.10% (mode 1) and 0.41% (mode 9) in closed form, and four cubic elements per arm are 0.03% (mode 1) to 0.45% (mode 9) high; at 16 elements per arm modes 10 and 11 are 1.20% low (and with the arms' area raised by 1e4 at the same I and mass per length every mode is within 0.002% of the target), so the -0.51% of 4 elements is that shortfall partly cancelled by the cubic mesh being up to 0.62% high
